channel.title: Solarhub Help Center
channel.description: Recent content on Solarhub Help Center

item.title: Collector
item.description: Function Overview linkThe collector is the core device for platform data access: on-site inverters, batteries, meters, optimizers and other sub-devices all hang under the collector, and the collector collects and reports their data to the platform in a unified way. So the collector must be imported first and then bound to a plant, and only then can the data of the sub-devices under it be displayed normally. 1. Device List link The device list can view online, faulty, offline and all device information.

item.title: Create Plant
item.description: Creation method 1 link Steps link Click the plus sign in the upper right corner of the plant list to enter the plant creation interface After adding the plant information, click the save button in the upper right corner to create successfully Creation method 2 link Steps link Click on the plant in the plant list to enter the plant overview interface Click Create Plant in the upper right corner menu After adding the plant information, click the Save button in the upper right corner to create successfully

item.title: Event Center
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Event Center summarizes the plants and devices that have alarmed on the platform: alarms and faults reported by devices generate an event record here. You can search by conditions, and create a work order to follow up on events that need handling. The list shows the plant name, device serial number, event time, event level, event code and event content of each event. The search box at the very top allows quick search by event content or device serial number.

item.title: Firmware Management
item.description: Function Overview linkPlatform device firmware management, including firmware search, adding firmware, modifying firmware, downloading firmware, access authorization, generating redemption codes, etc. Firmware is maintained separately by device type (collector, inverter, battery system, battery PACK, micro inverter, etc.). The list displays firmware name, firmware version, extended info, remark, file size and update time. When performing firmware upgrade in remote interaction and on the device details page, only the firmware that the current account has permission for and that matches the target device type will be seen.

item.title: Network Search Tool
item.description: Function Overview linkThe network search configuration tool is mainly used to configure the WiFi data stick (collector). Using the network search tool to send commands to the collector can modify the parameters of the collector Usage link1. Prerequisites linkThe PC using the network search tool must be in the same network as the collector, otherwise the collector will not be searched 2. Search for all collector devices in the current network link After opening the software, the network search tool will automatically find the gateway address of the current network as the search address by default.

item.title: Network Search Tool
item.description: Function Overview linkThe network search configuration tool is mainly used to configure the WiFi stick (collector). Sending commands to the collector with the network search tool can modify the parameters of the collector. The tool is a stand-alone program running on a PC (it is not a page of the platform). It is usually used for the configuration of a newly delivered collector and for on-site troubleshooting: first search for the collectors in the same network, then send AT commands to query or modify the configuration.

item.title: Organizational Structure
item.description: Function Overview linkOrganizational structure is used to manage the organizations, member accounts and measurement groups on the platform. The left side shows the organization tree; after selecting an organization, you can switch between Member List, Organization Information and Measurement Group on the right. Member List: view and manage the member accounts under the current organization Organization Information: view and modify the current organization, and create subordinate organizations Measurement Group: divide the device measurement points into groups to control which parameters a member can see on the device details page The organizations you can see and operate in the tree depend on your roles and permissions; subordinate organizations and their members are created and maintained by the superior organization.

item.title: Overview
item.description: Solarhub Web overview linkSolarhub Web provides comprehensive energy monitoring services for photovoltaic, wind power and energy storage systems, and offers professional and efficient comprehensive energy cloud monitoring platform services for medium and large plants, device manufacturers, O&M providers and residential plant owners. Main usage flow of the platform: Log in to the platform with an account (the account is created by the platform provider or by the administrator of your organization), see Login If you are responsible for on-site installation: first configure the network of the collector with the App, then import the collector, see Quick Start Create a plant and bind the collector to the plant, see Create Plant and Add Collector After the plant and the devices start to report data, use Data Dashboard, Plant Center and Device Center in daily work, and handle alarms and work orders in the Operation and Maintenance Center Get a Solarhub account link Trial account: to let you quickly experience the functions of Solarhub, we provide a customer trial account.

item.title: Plant Overview
item.description: Function Overview linkAfter entering the Plant User Perspective, the Plant Overview opens by default, showing the real-time power, generation, and estimated revenue of this plant. Page Content link Top: plant name, time of the latest data update (with time zone) Plant diagram: shows the current real-time power and the operating status of components such as PV and grid Generation: generation (kWh) for the four dimensions of today, this month, this year, and all Estimated Revenue: estimated revenue for today, this month, this year, and all (displayed in the currency unit configured on the platform) Common Operations link Upper right menu: Create Plant, Switch Plant, Add Logger, Network Configuration, Device List The bottom tabs switch among Overview, Statistics, Layout, and My Pull down the page to refresh the data Note: the overview data comes from the logger bound to this plant and its sub-devices.

item.title: Point Query
item.description: Function Overview linkQuery how a device reports measurement point data; the latest data reporting is displayed. It is used to troubleshoot device-side problems: for example, confirm whether the device is reporting, and whether the reported firmware version, server address, signal strength and other parameters meet expectations. The query result only reflects the latest data of the current day. The query result is displayed one by one by measurement point: Point ID: the number of the measurement point in the device type Measurement point name: the name of the measurement point (such as data update time, firmware version, Server Url, upload signal strength, etc.

item.title: Real-time Data
item.description: Function Overview linkAfter entering the Device User Perspective, the device details real-time data page opens by default, showing the current working status and parameters of this device. Page Content linkThe parameters shown differ by device type; take a Battery System as an example: SN: the device serial number SOC Status: remaining capacity, total voltage, etc. State of Health (SOH): battery health, cycle count System Power: current power and charge/discharge status (Charging/Discharging) Total Voltage, Battery Current and other real-time parameters Common Operations link Upper right menu: Refresh, Switch Device, Add Logger, Network Configuration, Parameter Settings, Device Alias, Unbind Device The bottom tabs switch among Real-time, Statistics, and My Pull down the page to refresh the data Note: the parameters an account can see are limited by the Measurement Group.

item.title: Registration And Login
item.description: 1. Account registration link Registration information overview: Email: used for account login and registration security code acquisition Security code: Enter a valid email address to send the security code Username: Platform users can use it as the platform account to log in Password: Platform account password Time zone: Account time zone. The platform will select different time zone offsets for time display based on the different account time zones Installer information: No need to change by default.

item.title: Summary Data
item.description: Function Overview linkSummary Data summarizes the day, month, year and total data of all plants and all devices, and you can filter the target data by conditions and then export it as an Excel sheet On the left you switch between “Plant report” and “Device report”. The filters shared by both pages are: Business Type: Select the business type to be counted (PV system, battery system, Residential Storage, etc.) Report Type: Day, month, year, total, which determines the granularity of the statistics and the data displayed Time: Select the corresponding date or time range according to the report type 1.

item.title: Switch Perspective
item.description: What is a perspective linkThe App provides three usage perspectives and the same account can switch between them at any time. The perspective decides what you see and what you can do: the landing page, the bottom navigation and the available entries are all different. Perspective Description in the App Who it is for Professional Consultant I am an equipment manufacturer, dealer, installer or professional consultant People who manage all plants and devices on the platform Plant User Focus on data with the plant as the focus People who only care about the data of a plant (e.

item.title: Batch Operation
item.description: Function Overview linkPerform parameter settings, firmware upgrade, command transmission and other operations on devices in batch. A batch operation is organized by “task”: first add devices to the task, then select the operation content and submit it. The platform executes device by device and counts the number of successes and failures; failed devices can be redone. Each row in the list displays the task’s failed/successful/processing/total counts, operation content, creator and creation time.

item.title: Collector not online at first power-on
item.description: Function Overview linkWhen the collector stays offline on the platform after installation and power-on, troubleshoot in the following order: first check the indicator lights of the device to make sure it starts normally, then use the network search configuration tool to check whether the server address configuration of the collector is correct. 1. Check the indicator light of the collector linkAfter power-on, first observe the indicator lights on the device to make sure it is powered and started normally (the meaning of each indicator light is described in the manual delivered with the device).

item.title: Device Statistics
item.description: Function Overview linkDevice Statistics is used to view the historical data curves of this device. Steps link On the device details page, tap the “Statistics” tab at the bottom Select the statistical dimension (such as day, month, year, or all) and the date The chart shows the data curve of this device in the selected time range; you can tap a data point to view the specific value Note: the selectable parameters are also limited by the measurement groups authorized to the account.

item.title: Inverter
item.description: Function Overview linkThe inverter is the power generation device that converts DC power into AC power; it usually hangs under a collector as a sub-device, and the collector collects and reports its operation data to the platform. 1. Device List link The device list can view online, faulty, offline and all device information; the status tabs at the top also show the device count of each status, and clicking a tab shows only the devices in that status.

item.title: Plant Statistics
item.description: Function Overview linkPlant Statistics is used to view the historical data of this plant: you can switch the statistical dimension by day, month, year, or all, and select a specific date or time range. Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the “Statistics” tab at the bottom Select the statistical dimension: day, month, year, or all (the selectable time range changes accordingly when you switch the dimension) Switch the date to view through the date selector; the chart will show the data curve of that time range Tap the zoom button in the upper right corner of the chart to view it in full screen Tap a point on the curve with the mouse/finger to view the specific value at that point Page Content link Chart area: the data curve of the selected dimension Below the chart: summary indicators such as peak power and full-load hours Note: after entering the details page of a plant in the Professional Consultant Perspective, there is also the same “Statistics” tab, with the same usage.

item.title: Quick Start
item.description: Solarhub App Overview link1. Registration and Login linkFor details, please refer to Registration and Login 2. Creating a Device linkNewly registered accounts need to create a device first. Click Create Device Add the device by scanning a QR code or entering the serial number manually Enter the network configuration interface Enter the Wi-Fi password to configure the network. During configuration, please make sure the device and the configuring phone are on the same 2.

item.title: Quick Start
item.description: Function Overview linkIf you are new to the platform, follow the five steps below to connect the on-site devices and see the data: Collector network configuration (use the App to connect the collector to the on-site WiFi) Collector import (add the collector to the platform) Create a plant Add collector (bind the collector to the plant) View plant and device data 1. Collector network configuration linkUse the Solarhub App to configure the network of the collector.

item.title: Search Or Filter Devices
item.description: 1. Device search link Under “Device” of the APP, you can search for devices by device serial number 2. Device filtering link Two conditions for filtering link Filter by device type Filter by device online status

item.title: Search Or Filter Events
item.description: 1. Event search link Under “Events” of the APP, you can search for events by event serial number 2. Event filtering link There are two states of events, occurring and recovered, which can be filtered by the title

item.title: Search Or Filter Plants
item.description: 1. Plant search link Under “Plant” of the App, you can search for plants by plant name keywords 2. Plant screening link Two conditions for filtering link Filter by plant type Filter by plant online status

item.title: The collector is not online when powered on for the first time
item.description: 1. Check the collector signal light link2. Use the network search configuration tool to check the configuration linkFor the usage of the network search configuration tool, refer to Network Search Configuration Tool 3. Check method link1. Query server selection link Send AT+SERVERSELECT command to query the URL selected in the service area. The firmware after version 3.0 points to URL2 by default, which is the address of each gateway service. If the address is unclear, please contact us.

item.title: Work Order Dashboard
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Work Order Dashboard is used to quickly understand the overall status of work orders: four key metrics at the top, a work order trend chart in the middle, and to-dos and score statistics below. Unresolved: the number of work orders that are not yet resolved Overdue: the number of work orders that have passed the first response or close deadline and are still unhandled, which need to be handled first Processing: the number of work orders being processed Unassigned: the number of work orders that have not been assigned to a handler Today’s Trend compares the change in the number of work orders between yesterday and today.

item.title: Add Logger
item.description: Steps link Select a plant in the plant list to enter the plant overview page Click Add Logger in the upper right corner of the plant overview page Scan the code or click the keyboard icon to enter the manual input interface Manually enter the logger SN number and click Add Device

item.title: Battery System
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Battery System (BMS) is the core device of an energy storage system; it usually hangs under a collector as a sub-device, and the collector collects and reports the operation data of the battery clusters and battery packs to the platform. 1. Device List link The device list can view online, faulty, offline and all device information; the status tabs at the top also show the device count of each status, and clicking a tab shows only the devices in that status.

item.title: Change Password
item.description: To change the password, you need to send a verification code to the account-bound email address After filling in the correct verification code, you can reset your password

item.title: Device Details
item.description: Entrance link Click on the device in the device list interface to enter the device overview page Function Overview linkThe menu at the top right of the device details page contains three operations: Parameter setting, Device alias, Unbind device (see below for details). The menu style is shown in the figure below. 1. Device Alias link 2. Remote upgrade link Moved to “My → OTA Assistant”: the device details menu of the new version of the App no longer provides a remote upgrade entry.

item.title: Event Details
item.description: Click the event at the bottom of the APP to enter the event interface Click the event in the event list to enter the event details interface View the event details

item.title: Login
item.description: Function Overview linkLog in to Solarhub (Web) with a platform account. After a successful login the data dashboard page is shown. Visit the Solarhub login page through Solarhub, enter the correct account and password and log in App download: the upper right corner of the login page provides the App download QR code; scan it with your phone to download the latest App released by the platform Multi-language switch: the upper right corner of the login page allows you to switch the display language After a successful login the data dashboard page is shown

item.title: Plant Layout
item.description: Function Overview linkPlant Layout is used to view the physical layout and connection relationships of the modules/devices in this plant, as well as the power curve corresponding to the layout. 1. Create Layout link Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the “Layout” tab at the bottom When the plant has no layout yet, the page shows a “Create Layout” button; after tapping it, the platform automatically generates the corresponding components based on the devices under the plant After generation, you can drag components to adjust their positions, or tap “Edit” below to edit a single component (adjust its direction and angle).

item.title: Switch Device
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Device User Perspective focuses on only one device at a time. When you need to view another device, use “Switch Device”. Steps link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner Select “Switch Device” Select the device you want to view in the device list, and you will enter the details page of that device Note: this is an entry unique to the Device User Perspective.

item.title: Work Order List
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Work Order List shows all work orders and is divided into several tabs by the relationship with the current account: Created by me: work orders created by the current account To-do: work orders that need to be handled by the current account Related to me: work orders that the current account has participated in (such as being replied to or copied) All: all work orders within the data permissions of the current account The information in the list includes the work order number, subject, work order type, handler (or creator), first response deadline, close deadline, priority, status and operations.

item.title: Account Cancellation
item.description: When an account is deactivated or no longer used, you can delete the account information by canceling the account. At this time, all data generated by the account on the platform will be cleared

item.title: Add Logger
item.description: Function Overview linkYou can also add a logger directly in the Device User Perspective: the entry is in the menu in the upper right corner of the device details page. Steps link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner and select “Add Logger” Scan the logger QR code, or tap the keyboard icon to manually enter the logger serial number After entering it, tap “Add Device” Note: this is an entry unique to the Device User Perspective (there is no Add Logger in the device details of the Professional Consultant Perspective); the logger must first be imported on the platform.

item.title: Customer Team
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Customer Team is used to divide the teams that handle work orders: each team has a name, description, main responsibilities and main members, and work orders are assigned to the corresponding team according to the team’s main responsibilities. The list shows the team name, description, main responsibilities (tags such as complaint, problem, return or exchange) and main members. The operation column allows you to modify or dissolve a team.

item.title: Device Statistics
item.description: Click a device in the device list to enter the device details Click to enter Statistics from the menu below (before the version update, this tab was named “History”) Statistics support four views: day, month, year, and all In the chart, you can view the data at a certain point in time by continuously pressing

item.title: Multi-language Switch
item.description: Function Overview linkThe platform supports multiple interface languages, which can be switched at any time before or after login; the switch takes effect immediately. Before login, switch the language through the icon in the upper right corner After login, switch the language next to the user in the upper right corner Multi-language texts on the platform (for example the name of a measurement group or the name of a device parameter) are shown in the corresponding language when the interface language is switched; if a name is not filled in for that language, the default name is shown.

item.title: Network Configuration
item.description: Function Overview linkTap “Network Configuration” in the menu in the upper right corner of the device details page to configure the WiFi network the logger should connect to. The logger can connect to the server and report data only after the network configuration succeeds. How to Use link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner and select “Network Configuration” to enter the network configuration interface Tap add device in the upper right corner, and add the logger to be configured by scanning the code or manually entering the serial number The device can be checked only when the logger has entered the network configuration state; after checking it, you enter the Wi-Fi selection interface Select the 2.

item.title: Optimizer
item.description: Function Overview linkThe optimizer (MLPE) is used to perform independent maximum power point tracking for every module in a PV string; it usually hangs under a collector as a sub-device, and the collector collects and reports its data to the platform. 1. Device List link The device list can view online, faulty, offline and all device information; the status tabs at the top also show the device count of each status, and clicking a tab shows only the devices in that status.

item.title: Remote Interaction
item.description: Function Overview linkSend downlink commands to the collector, including firmware upgrade (OTA), command transmission and parameter settings. The remote interaction interface displays the currently online collectors by default, and can also perform advanced search by serial number, status, plant, tag and firmware version. Each row in the list corresponds to a collector, showing status, serial number, brand, model, plant, signal strength, communication type, timezone and data update time. The operation column provides four entries: firmware upgrade, operation log, command transmission and parameter settings.

item.title: Switch Plant
item.description: Steps link Select a plant in the plant list to enter the plant overview page Click Switch Plant in the upper right corner of the plant overview page to enter the switch plant interface Select the plant to switch to complete the switch

item.title: Switch Plant
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Plant User Perspective focuses on only one plant at a time. When you need to view another plant, use “Switch Plant” to switch. Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the menu in the upper right corner Select “Switch Plant” Select the plant to switch to in the plant list, and you will enter that plant’s overview page Note: the list only shows plants within the data permissions of the current account.

item.title: Create Plant
item.description: Function Overview linkYou can also create a plant in the Plant User Perspective: the entry is in the menu in the upper right corner of the plant overview page. Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the menu in the upper right corner and select “Create Plant” Fill in basic information such as the plant name Tap the save button in the upper right corner to complete creation After successful creation, you can switch to the newly created plant in “Switch Plant” For more complete instructions on creating a plant (including fields such as plant type, installed capacity, and location), see Create Plant.

item.title: Data Dashboard
item.description: Function Overview linkThe data dashboard is the default home page after logging in. It shows the plant situation within the data permissions of the current account from a macro point of view: the total number of plants, the number of plants of each type, and the geographic distribution of the plants. There are also two shortcuts in the upper right corner of the page: My work orders: go to the Work Order List to see the work orders related to you My favorites: quickly open the plants you follow (click the star in front of the plant name in the plant list to follow a plant) Business use link As an O&M provider or installer, you need to know the category and number of plants connected to your company and the device distribution.

item.title: Device Event
item.description: Click a device in the device list to enter the device details Click to enter the event from the menu below Events have two states: Occurring and Recovered. You can filter by clicking the title above Click on an event to view detailed information about the event

item.title: Network Configuration
item.description: Go to “My” at the bottom of the APP and click Network Configuration to enter the network configuration interface and prepare for network configuration To configure the network, you need to turn on Bluetooth, connect to 2.4GhzWIFi, and authorize Bluetooth WiFi and other permissions to the APP, otherwise the network configuration may fail. Add a device in the upper right corner, add a device by scanning the code or manually entering the serial number If the device enters the network configuration state, it will appear to be checked.

item.title: Notice Announcement
item.description: Function Overview linkPush announcement messages on the Web or App, used to publish notices to users (such as maintenance notices and activity notices). The list displays the title, type, status, creator and creation time of published announcements, and supports searching by title, publisher and type; the operation column allows you to modify or delete an announcement. Click “Add” to create an announcement, which requires filling in: Title: the title of the announcement, required Type: App notification push (pushed to the App) or system announcement (displayed on the platform) Publisher: the name of the announcement publisher Content: the body of the announcement Push Scope: full push (all users), end user group (end users only) or specific users (specified accounts) After saving, the announcement is pushed to the corresponding users according to the selected scope.

item.title: Parameter Settings
item.description: Function Overview linkTap “Parameter Settings” in the menu in the upper right corner of the device details page to deliver writable parameters to the current device (different device types support different parameters). Steps link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner Select “Parameter Settings” Select or enter the parameters to be delivered on the parameter page Tap the deliver button to execute (multiple parameters can be delivered at one time) Notes link Parameters are delivered directly to the device on site; please make sure the device is online and the parameter values are correct The delivery result can be viewed on the device details page of the Web platform (or in the device operation log) Delivery fails or times out when the device is offline

item.title: Plant Statistics
item.description: Steps link Select a plant in the plant list to enter the plant overview interface Select Statistics at the bottom to enter the statistics interface (this tab was named “History” before the version update) You can view the data at a certain time point by pressing the chart You can switch the data of the previous day or the next day by using the arrow above, and click the time to manually select the time; the zoom-in button in the upper right corner of the chart allows full-screen viewing

item.title: Production Test
item.description: Function Overview linkUse production test to test whether a device meets a certain test standard. Production test is divided into three parts, corresponding to the three tabs on the page: Test Standard: define “what to measure and what condition counts as passing” Task List: create test tasks for devices and track their running status Test Record: the entry for querying historical test tasks and reports 1. Create Test Standard link Select the device type to be tested, select the measurement points, aggregate functions, test conditions and thresholds for testing devices of this type, and save the test standard.

item.title: Smart Meter
item.description: Function Overview linkThe meter is used to measure the energy data of a plant such as the grid connection and the load; it usually hangs under a collector as a sub-device, and the collector collects and reports its data to the platform. 1. Device List link The device list can view online, faulty, offline and all device information; the status tabs at the top also show the device count of each status, and clicking a tab shows only the devices in that status.

item.title: Add Logger
item.description: Function Overview linkBind the logger to the current plant, and only then will the plant start to have data. The entry is in the menu in the upper right corner of the plant overview page. Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the menu in the upper right corner and select “Add Logger” After entering the scan page, scan the QR code on the logger with your phone; if you cannot find the QR code on the logger, you can tap “Didn’t find the serial number?

item.title: Device Alias
item.description: Function Overview linkTap “Device Alias” in the menu in the upper right corner of the device details page to give the device an easily recognizable name. The alias is shown in the device list, the device details and other places. Steps link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner Select “Device Alias” Enter the new alias Tap save in the upper right corner; the alias takes effect immediately Note: the alias only affects the displayed name and does not change the device serial number.

item.title: Local Debugging
item.description: Template engine rendering link Click local debugging in the “My” interface at the bottom of the APP After the APP enters the local debugging function for the first time, it will automatically download the template rendering engine to load the template data. The template engine will iterate and have more powerful functions, which can be updated at any time in subsequent use Template Management link When you first enter local debugging, the latest template will be automatically downloaded.

item.title: OTA Assistant
item.description: Click OTA Assistant in the “My” interface at the bottom of the APP The firmware redeemed with the redemption code will be displayed in the list Click Redeem in the upper right corner to redeem the firmware with the redemption code. For redemption code generation, refer to the Web Click Firmware Upgrade to enter the upgrade interface Select the device to be upgraded, and the list will display the online devices under the plant in the current plant overview for upgrade

item.title: Plant Layout
item.description: 1. Create layout link Steps link Select a plant in the plant list to enter the plant overview interface Select Layout at the bottom to enter the layout interface Create a layout By default, corresponding components will be created based on all devices under the plant 2. Edit layout link Steps link You can freely adjust the position of components by dragging them or edit them individually through the edit below

item.title: PVS
item.description: Function Overview linkThe PVS page is used to manage plants whose business type is PVS: the plant overview metrics are at the top, and below you can view and find plants through the two tabs “Plant List” and “Plant Map”; click a plant to enter its details page. “Add Plant” and “System large screen” in the upper right corner of the page are used to create a plant and display in full screen respectively.

item.title: Battery System
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Battery System page is used to manage plants whose business type is Battery System. Its page structure is the same as the PVS (overview, list, map, System large screen, details page); the difference is that the overview metrics and the details page charts summarize charge and discharge data. Plant Overview link The plant overview of the Battery System includes four sections: real-time power, Charge/Discharge Statistics, social benefits, and online plants.

item.title: Plant Device List
item.description: Function Overview linkTo view devices in the Plant User Perspective: select “Device List” in the menu in the upper right corner of the plant overview page. Difference from the Professional Consultant Perspective link Plant User Perspective: the device list only shows the devices under the current plant, suitable for users who only view the devices of their own plant Professional Consultant Perspective: the “Device” tab at the bottom shows all devices, allowing filtering across plants by logger and device status, and searching by serial number Steps link On the plant overview page, tap the menu in the upper right corner and select “Device List” The page shows the devices under the current plant (loggers and their sub-devices), which can be filtered by device type and status Tap a device card to enter the details page of that device Note: if there are no devices under the plant yet, the page will show “No data”; in that case you need to bind a logger to the plant through “Add Logger”.

item.title: Unbind Device
item.description: Function Overview linkTap “Unbind Device” in the menu in the upper right corner of the device details page to remove the binding relationship between the device and the plant (or between a sub-device and the logger). Steps link On the device details page, tap the menu in the upper right corner Select “Unbind Device” Confirm the prompt to complete unbinding Notes link Unbinding a sub-device deletes the sub-device from the logger and clears the data of the sub-device; please operate with care After a logger is unbound, its binding relationship with the plant is removed, and it needs to be added again to continue reporting data Unbinding cannot be undone

item.title: Residential Storage
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Residential Storage page is used to manage plants whose business type is Residential Storage. This type of plant contains both photovoltaic power generation and battery storage, so the overview and charts display the data of power generation, power consumption, power grid and battery at the same time. Plant Overview link The plant overview of the Residential Storage includes four sections: power generation, power grid, battery, and power consumption.

item.title: Commercial Plant
item.description: Function Overview linkThe Commercial Plant page is used to manage plants whose business type is Commercial Plant (EMS). Its page structure is exactly the same as the PVS: the plant overview is at the top, the plant list and plant map are below, you can add a plant and enter the System large screen in the upper right corner, and click a plant to enter its details page. For the specific description of each section, please refer to the corresponding chapter; this section only lists the differences from the PVS and Residential Storage.

item.title: Create Plant
item.description: Function Overview linkCreating a plant means entering a plant into the platform and filling in its Installed Capacity, address coordinates, owner, visitors, and other information. After creation, the plant appears in the Plant List, and once a collector is bound, the Power Generation data becomes available. 1. Create Entry link Click “Add Plant” in the upper right corner of the page for the corresponding business type in the Plant Center, and complete the wizard in four steps: Basic Information → Geographic Location → Stakeholders → Photos.

item.title: Modify Plant
item.description: Function Overview linkModifying a plant is used to update the plant’s basic information, location, stakeholders and photos. Errors made when creating the plant, or changes that occur later (for example, a changed contact, or the need to authorize a new visitor), are all adjusted here. 1. Modify Plant Entry link Click “Modify” in the operation column on the right side of the Plant List (you can also enter from the plant details page)

item.title: Visitor Authorization
item.description: Function Overview linkVisitor Authorization grants the viewing permission of a plant to other accounts on the platform. The authorized account (visitor) can see this plant in its own Plant List and view its data, but cannot modify or delete the plant — management operations such as modifying, deleting and adding a collector can still only be performed by the plant owner. Multiple visitors can be added to one plant; deleting a visitor revokes that account’s viewing permission.

item.title: Add Collector
item.description: Function Overview linkAdding a collector means binding a collector to a plant. The data reported by the collector is attributed to this plant, and only then do indicators such as the plant’s Real-time Power and Power Generation have data. Two conditions must be met before adding: The collector has already completed Collector import in “Device Center → Collector”; a serial number that has not been imported will prompt “SN verification failed” The serial number is not duplicated; a serial number that has already been added will prompt “Serial number already exists” There are two ways to add: enter a single serial number, or add in bulk via a template file.
